pr_title: [Image Resizer] Fix image resizer unexpected property type or value (#9885, #14266)
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

**What is this about:**

Improves resilience of the image resize implementation.

This PR fixes different categories of bugs in described in #9885 and #14266.

Bug category 1:
- Image contains partially invalid metadata which throws an exception on:
  - reading a given metadata field
  - writing metadata to a given field or persisting the image containing the metadata to disk. 

Bug category 2:
- Some metadata depends on the availability of a thumbnail image. The encoder crashes if the thumbnail image is not found.

**What is include in the PR:** 
- Loop over all metadata and try to read the actual value. Remove metadata item if exception is thrown while reading the value. Build up the metadata object from the scratch by adding all valid values. This resolves Bug category 1
- copy thumbnail image from input to output image to resolve Bug category 2
- Adds two metadata debug methods to simplify the debugging of metadata related bugs 

**How does someone test / validate:** 
test with images provided in linked issue.

Images: Bug category 1:
[#9885 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9885#issuecomment-958967927)
[#9885 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9885#issuecomment-891829849)
[#14266 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/14266#issue-1044400800)

Images: Bug category 2:
[#9885 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9885#issue-815762941)

## Quality Checklist

- [x] **Linked issue:** #9885, #14266
- [x] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors in the issue. 
- [ ] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass
- [ ] **Installer:** Added/updated and all pass
- [ ] **Localization:** All end user facing strings can be localized
- [ ] **Docs:** Added/ updated
- [ ] **Binaries:** Any new files are added to WXS / YML

**My thoughts on your code:**
I think we should log a warning if we remove corrupt metadata while resizing. This helps us on incomming issues because the normal logs aren't debug logs.

I suggest something like this:
```
[Warn] Removing corrupt metadata property <name> from image <path>. - Reason: <reason of corruption>
```

- "Remove metadata that doesn't affect rendering option"
- "Remove metadata which causes problems in some cases" ?

> > Can this be made into an option, as suggested [in the original proposal](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9885#issuecomment-969355640)? "Remove metadata which causes problems in some cases"

> > The adding a thumbnail change is good and can stay even if the option is not selected.
> > Other than that, it looks great to me!
> 
> We already have "Remove metadata that doesn't affect rendering option" which make ImageResizer work for images mentioned in this issue.. Do we want to have both
> 
> * "Remove metadata that doesn't affect rendering option"
> * "Remove metadata which causes problems in some cases" ?

In the issue some users mentioned that they still wanted some metadata regarding camera settings, while not wanting to hit these errors for those images.

As the one who started the original thread https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9885#issuecomment-890903077  back in February, I can say I would not use Image Resizer (fantasic and easy-to-use as it is!) if it removed EXIF tags that are important to photographers referring back to what was going on with their images. In particular, tags dealing with make model of the camera and lens, orientation, exposure time, FNumber, ExposureProgram, ISOSpeedRatings, DateTimeOriginal, OffsetTime, ExposureBiasValue, MeteringMode, FocalLength, CoilorSpace, Flash, any GPS info. Another few that I believe are used by some programs to decide how to display or print the image are XResolution, YResolution, and ResolutionUnit. I don't know what a lot of the other tags are used for, so I don't know if they are important or not for some obscure reason.

Going back to the other thread,

**I am not a coder!!**, so I don't know if this is practical or possible or too much work. I wonder if an alternative might be to use the code within - https://sourceforge.net/projects/jpegview/ that writes the metadata. It seems to have no problems handling the metadata in the problem images I have (which start as Nikon NEF RAW files and were saved as JPG files by various programs)

My problem images all started as Nikon RAW (.NEF) files. (but others have indicated it has been a problem with their non-Nikon files. serafisnz mentioned in the other thread that he uses a Sony camera.)

- ON1 Photo RAW exports a JPG but the metadata in the resulting export still causes Image Resizer to choke
- IrfanView exports a JPG but the metadata in the resulting export still causes Image Resizer to choke
- PhotoScape X exports a JPG ... AND seems to fix the metadata - Image Resizer can process it fine

So other programs are managing to write JPG files even if the property values are "bad". ON1 Photo RAW, Irfanview, and PhotoScape X are not open source so it is not possible to see how they are doing it, but JPEGVIEW can write JPG files that have such "bad" EXIF data and it is open source. So if it would be possible to use whatever technique they are using to write EXIF data, I think the issue here could be considered solved.

Otherwise, if it is not possible to change the code that writes the EXIF info, I think it is really important to preserve as much "good" EXIF info as possible.

Thanks.

0.49.1

### Running as admin

- [X] Yes

### Area(s) with issue?

Image Resizer

### Steps to reproduce

Try to resize this image - https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/Textures/jpg/4k/rock_boulder_dry/rock_boulder_dry_ao_4k.jpg

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

_No response_

### ❌ Actual Behavior

I get an error: The following images cannot be resized (Original - "Невозможно изменить размер следующих изображений")

_No response_
